title: Routed exact-key BSGS for fixed-G1 pairing inversion

claims.statement: For every nonidentity P in G1 and every z in GT, D=e(P,Q0) generates GT and z=D^a. Baby-step/giant-step with m=h=2^128, exact 72-limb keys, 256-bit indexes and a routed binary memory tree recovers a and returns Q=[a]Q0, with infinity when z=1. There are no heuristics. Success probability is 1. Total classical work is at most 2^145 dense-Fp12 units at C=20000, including tree installation, both lists, merge-sort, binary search, failed giant steps, the pairing, the G2 scalar and verification. Peak memory is below 2^150 bytes. Advice is 0 bytes.

experiments.purpose: Recover every exponent in a 100-element toy group by exact-key BSGS, and check the production instruction inequalities.
